category_title: Students exhibiting severe emotional behavioural difficulties (EBD)
minimal_context: The student is participating in regular classroom work with the whole class and is expected to complete an independent reading assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Class, please open your textbooks to page 42 and complete the reading assignment quietly at your desks.

STUDENT: I don't want to read this. Everyone is staring at me like there is something different about me. I don't feel like I am part of the group.

TUTOR: Just look at the book and try your best to read it.

STUDENT: (Starts acting out and pacing around the classroom) I'm not doing it! I hate this!

TUTOR: Please sit back down and be quiet, I need to help the other students right now.

STUDENT: (Suddenly hits another pupil severely who is sitting nearby) Get away from me!

options.A: Frequently acknowledge achievements during the reading assignment while ensuring the academic demands remain within the student's capability.
options.B: Use music as a means for theoretical learning, enjoyment, peer interaction, relaxation, and as a reward.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each reading task during the independent classroom assignment.
options.D: Organize classroom work around the student exhibiting behavioral difficulties, utilizing extensive planning and a highly structured environment.
